citation: Zhu, Chen, Dou, Li, Guo, Chen & Zhang (2025), arXiv 2504.15716v1 (DianJin-R1). Read: abstract page and v1 HTML (tables 1-6)
text_source: DianJin-R1-Data: CFLUE MCQ 26,672 and open-ended 5,045 (Chinese), FinQA 4,851, in-house CCC compliance dialogues 1,800; DeepSeek-R1 chains, GPT-4o verified; CCC chains from a Qwen2.5-72B multi-agent workflow of condition nodes merged by GPT-4o
feature: Financial MCQ, numeric QA, binary compliance check (violation or not) from a dialogue; answer accuracy only
method: Qwen2.5-7B/32B-Instruct: SFT on verified chains, then GRPO (format + accuracy reward on CFLUE MCQ only)
outcome: 7B: CFLUE 69.4 to 80.3, FinQA 66.7 to 77.7 (SFT-only 80.3; RL -2.6), CCC 55.0 to 94.5 in one call vs 72B multi-agent 95.0 at 8.15 calls and 72B single 55.5; R1-Distill-Qwen-7B below instruct on all finance sets (CFLUE 48.4, CCC 41.5)
incremental_to: Instruct bases; DeepSeek-R1; QwQ-32B; R1-distilled Qwen 7B-32B; Qwen2.5-72B multi-agent
pit_handling: Not addressed; CCC test (200) from same in-house pool and guidelines; FinQA train/test overlap unchecked
informs_decision: Strongest evidence that an explicit procedure (graph of condition nodes run by a large model, merged into one chain) can be distilled into a 7B single call, in distribution. Template for S1 teacher data: run a fixed analysis graph, check each node against XBRL, merge. No held-out test of the workflow

citation: Zhao, Zhou, Chen, Wang, Huang and 10 others (2025), arXiv 2507.12901v3 (Agentar-DeepFinance-100K). Read: abstract page and v3 HTML (tables 1-6)
text_source: About 100-115K mostly Chinese finance items (FinCorpus, FinCUGE, Finance-Instruct-500K, FinQA 5,012, in-house FinCAS 15,190, FinRA); six task domains; QwQ-Plus chains; quality score >= 8; answer-checked by an unnamed light model
feature: Chain-of-thought synthesis choices: chain or none, by difficulty and task type; chain length; which model writes the chain; repair of failed items
method: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct SFT on a 60K subset, 3 epochs, per condition ('CoT Cube')
outcome: Answer-only on hard items falls below base (Fin-Eva 83.7 to 75.8); with chain 86.0. By task (held-out 10%): Math 31.7 to 61.2, Analysis & Interpretation 81.4 to 88.1, NLP 76.7 to 77.2. Best teacher (R1, FinQA 75.4) gives a worse student (66.5) than QwQ-Plus (73.0; student 68.8). Long > short chains at 7B (FinQA 68.8 vs 65.6). Repairing 862 failed items +1.74 FinQA
incremental_to: Base model; chains vs answer-only; three chain writers; three chain lengths
pit_handling: Overlap with benchmark test sets 'removed' (method, counts not given); FinQA both a source and a test set
informs_decision: Train R-d on rationale plus answer, never answer-only (EXP-0050's boxed-number collapse is the same shape). Pick the teacher by the student's dev score, not the teacher's. Chain length is an experiment at 0.8B (contrast li-2025). One 7B student only

citation: Xiao, Sun, Chen, Wu, Luo & Wang (2025), arXiv 2509.11420v1 (Trading-R1, Tauric Research). Read: abstract page and v1 HTML (main text and reward appendix)
text_source: Tauric-TR1-DB about 100K samples: 14 large-cap equities and ETFs, Jan 2024-May 2025; news, prices and indicators, fundamentals and SEC filings, insider/analyst sentiment, macro; 20-30K-token inputs; theses 6-8K tokens
feature: Structured investment thesis (sections, opinion-quote-source bullets, tables) ending in a 5-class rating; labels from volatility-adjusted 3/7/15-day forward returns
method: Qwen3-4B; 'reverse reasoning distillation' (o3-mini/o4-mini give only the rating, a planner writes the steps backwards, GPT-4.1-nano expands); 3-stage curriculum structure -> claims -> decision, each SFT + GRPO + rejection sampling; rewards count sections, quotes, sources, and a payoff matrix
outcome: Jun-Aug 2024, 6 tickers: CR/Sharpe e.g. NVDA 8.08/2.72, AAPL 5.82/1.80 vs SFT-only -2.37/-1.27; larger models win some cells (Qwen3-32B Sharpe 2.12 vs 1.72 on AMZN); no measure of thesis quality or hallucination
incremental_to: SFT-only, RL-only; Qwen3-4B/32B, GPT-4.1 family, Llama-3.3, o3/o4-mini
pit_handling: Claimed point-in-time inputs; but the test window lies inside the stated data window and exclusion is not shown; cutoffs not discussed: contaminated or bounded at best
informs_decision: Only 4B finance 'analyst' model found. Gives a data shape for a framework (fixed sections, claim-quote-source, decision) but rewards check form, not truth, and rationales are written backwards from the label (rationalisation risk, cf. turpin-2023). S1 should run the procedure forward and verify each claim

citation: Wu, Zou, Wang, Wang, Yang & Shao (2025), arXiv 2506.07315v2 (FinAR-Bench). Read: abstract page and v2 HTML (tables 1-8)
text_source: Statements of 100 Shanghai-listed firms, FY2023 with FY2022 comparatives, as XBRL-derived text and PDF pages; 32 line items, 38 indicators, 64 trend/threshold/comparison conditions
feature: Financial statement analysis split into checkable steps: extraction, indicator calculation, condition table, then narrative
method: 14 models in three size groups, zero-shot; formulas-in-prompt arm; tables scored by key matching with relative-error threshold; narrative by LLM-judge tournament (large models only)
outcome: Under 10B: extraction precision 38-66 vs 97-100 for large; indicator recall at 5% tolerance Qwen2.5-7B 46.6, Mistral-7B 18.9 vs GPT-o1 90.6, DeepSeek-R1 88.0 (exact-match 2-9 vs 34-49); conditions about 50-58 vs 63-86; formulas help medium/large, 'minimal or even negative' for small
incremental_to: Size groups; with vs without formulas; text vs PDF
pit_handling: Not addressed; labels computed from filed statements (no outcome recall); FY2023 reports may be in pretraining data
informs_decision: Gives S1 a judge-free decomposition of a framework (extract, compute, condition table, interpret) and a release-level condition table as a 'whole framework' test. Grade numbers with tolerance. Matches EXP-0050: hints do not rescue small models. Needs a chance baseline

citation: Sugiura, Ishida, Makino, Tazuke, Nakagawa, Nakago & Ha (2026), ICLR 2026; arXiv 2506.08762v2 (EDINET-Bench). Read: abstract page and v2 HTML
text_source: 41,691 Japanese annual reports (EDINET) 2014-2025; fraud set 534/555 from amended reports (LLM-labelled amendment reasons, manually reviewed); earnings set 1,000 firm-year pairs, time split at 2020
feature: Fraud detection (restatement-derived) and sign of next-year profit change from one whole report (~30K tokens); tables vs tables plus text
method: Zero-shot frontier and open LLMs (3 runs); Llama-3.2-1B SFT; logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost on the same figures
outcome: Earnings direction AUC mostly 0.40-0.62, best GPT-5 0.65 (MCC 0.21), LR 0.56, 1B SFT 0.48-0.52; fraud best LLM 0.73 (Claude 3.5 Sonnet with text) vs random forest 0.75 on summary table; 1B SFT 0.66 on tables, 0.54 with text
incremental_to: Classical classifiers on summary figures; input configurations
pit_handling: Partly: name-guessing from tables <= 0.05; no fraud decline in recent years; cutoffs not stated; earnings test years (2020+) pre-cutoff, bounded at best
informs_decision: Outcome-checkable judgements from filings are near chance for most LLMs and for a 1B fine-tuned model: keep S1 R4 secondary. Restatement labels are a verifiable non-revision signal (EDGAR analogue: 8-K Item 4.02, 10-K/A). Prose can hurt small models; tree baseline matches best LLM

citation: Zheng, Du, Liao, Zhao, Zhou and 8 others (2025), arXiv 2507.16802v4 (Agentar-Fin-R1). Read: abstract page and v4 HTML (tables 1-5)
text_source: About 300K SFT samples: label-guided synthetic finance tasks (multi-agent synthesis, unnamed teachers), Agentar-DeepFinance data, general sets (Llama-Nemotron, OpenThoughts); mostly Chinese
feature: Finova (own; 1,350 items: agent intent/slot/tool/expression 868, complex reasoning 282, safety and compliance 200), FinEval, FinanceIQ; grading not described
method: Qwen3-8B/32B; label-guided difficulty-aware SFT then GRPO
outcome: 8B: Finova 54.5 to 63.6 (complex reasoning 48.6 to 51.6; expression 32 to 63), FinEval 76.3 to 85.1; MATH-500 93.8 to 93.4. Older specialists far below a newer base: Fin-R1 fin avg 55.3, DianJin-R1-7B 63.2 vs Qwen3-8B 67.9
incremental_to: Qwen3 bases; DeepSeek-R1; o1; Fin-R1; DianJin-R1; XuanYuan-FinX1
pit_handling: Dedup and benchmark-overlap removal described, no counts; Finova is the authors' own benchmark
informs_decision: Gains largest on agent formatting tasks, smallest on complex reasoning (+3.1 at 8B). A newer general base beats last year's finance specialist: S1 should compare against the untuned base of the same generation

citation: Cao, Lin, Zhong, Gao, Cai, He, Han & Wu (2026), arXiv 2603.07223v1 (ODA-Fin). Read: abstract page and v1 HTML (tables 1-4)
text_source: ODA-Fin-SFT-318k from 697K-946K raw items in 25+ open sets; chains by Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking; ODA-Fin-RL-12k hard verifiable items (SFT model fails >= 2 of 4); CompassVerifier-7B rewards
feature: Nine benchmarks: FinEval, Finova, FinanceIQ, FOMC, FPB, Headlines, FinQA, TaTQA, ConvFinQA
method: Qwen3-8B and Qwen2.5-7B: SFT (raw answers vs partial vs full distilled chains), then GRPO with answer-length caps
outcome: Qwen3-8B avg: base 71.5; raw-answer SFT 66.1; full-chain SFT 72.1 (below base on 6 of 9 incl. FinQA 69.8 vs 72.2); +RL 74.6 = Qwen3-32B base 74.7. RL from base 68.4
incremental_to: Base; raw vs partial vs full chains; verifier types and caps; DianJin-R1-7B, Fin-R1
pit_handling: No decontamination against the nine eval sets reported
informs_decision: On a strong modern base, distilled-chain SFT barely moves the average and answer-only SFT hurts; RL on hard verifiable short answers adds 2.5. For a Qwen3.5 student, expect small SFT gains on familiar tasks; gains must be shown on S1's own items

citation: Zhu, Zhou, Jiang, Li, Guo, Chen & Zhang (2026), IJCAI 2026; arXiv 2508.15202v2 (Fin-PRM). Read: abstract page and v2 HTML
text_source: 3,000 DeepSeek-R1 trajectories on CFLUE; step labels from Monte Carlo rollouts (Qwen2.5-7B-Math), Qwen3-235B judge, knowledge-base check

method: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct policy: PRM-selected SFT data, Best-of-N, GRPO reward shaping
outcome: SFT on top-1,000 PRM-selected trajectories: CFLUE 45.3 to 58.2 (Math-PRM-72B 57.1; random selection 43.8); RL +3.3 over outcome-only reward (CFLUE 70.5, FinQA 62.8); BoN beats majority vote by >5.1 at N=16

citation: Huang & Simpson (2026), LREC 2026, pp. 10242-10254; arXiv 2606.18875v1. Read: abstract page and v1 HTML

citation: Lu, Guo, Zhang, Zhu & Liu (2025), arXiv 2505.19457v1 (BizFinBench). Read: abstract page and v1 HTML (Table 3, grading, judge ablation)
text_source: 6,781 Chinese queries from a finance app (iwencai), context from databases with distractors; three experts, full consensus
feature: Nine task types: anomalous event attribution, numerical computation, time reasoning, tool use, knowledge QA, data description, emotion, stock prediction, entity recognition
method: 25 models zero-shot incl. Qwen3-1.7B/4B/14B/32B; accuracy for six tasks, GPT-4o judge for three; IteraJudge
outcome: Qwen3 1.7B/4B/14B/32B: event attribution 77.4/83.6/84.2/83.8; numeric 35.8/47.4/58.2/59.6; time reasoning 33.4/50.0/65.8/64.6; entity recognition 11.2/25.2/50.7/49.2; data description 78.6/80.2/92.9/95.4; stock prediction 48.5-52.3 (flat); avg 50.8/59.9/67.1/68.3
incremental_to: Size within Qwen3; open vs closed
pit_handling: Queries time-anchored with misaligned distractors; contamination not discussed
informs_decision: Within one family: classification-like attribution saturates by 4B; numeric, time (period) reasoning and extraction keep scaling to 14B. S1's derived-period and extraction steps are where the 0.8B will lag. Judge ablation: Spearman 0.31-0.57 on data description and 0.70-0.87 on tool use (reference of the correlation not confirmed in the text read)

citation: Dou, Shen, Chen, Wang, Xu and 7 others (2025), FinNLP@EMNLP 2025; arXiv 2506.21591v3 (FinEval-KR). Read: abstract page and v3 HTML (Table 7, method)
text_source: 9,782 Chinese financial reasoning QA, 22 subfields, built with o1
feature: Decouples knowledge from reasoning: re-answer with missing knowledge supplied; Bloom-level cognitive scores
method: Qwen2.5-72B judge identifies first wrong step; knowledge injected; error attributed to knowledge or reasoning
outcome: Acc / KS / RS: Fin-R1-7B 0.42/0.75/0.56; Qwen2.5-14B 0.55/0.85/0.69; GPT-4o 0.69/0.90/0.81; DeepSeek-R1 0.87/0.95/0.93. 'Apply' level lowest for all (GPT-4.1 0.79 vs 0.89 analyse). Removing key knowledge cut Qwen2.5-7B and GPT-4o by about 28%; expert check of pipeline 0.92-0.94
incremental_to: General vs financial LLMs; with vs without knowledge

citation: Zhu and 20 others (2025-2026), arXiv 2510.13936 (FinDeepResearch, HisRubric). Read: abstract page (v2, 7 Jan 2026) and v1 HTML
text_source: Annual reports and market data for 64 listed firms, 8 markets, 4 languages; 247 grading items per report (15,808 total); references by LLM majority vote then two expert rounds
feature: Corporate analysis report in 6 sections; items at four levels: Recognition, Calculation (1 mark), Abstraction, Interpretation (2 marks)
method: 16 methods (deep-research agents, LLMs with thinking and search); unnamed LLM judge: binary accuracy, claim coverage (3-5 claims), generated 10-point criteria; rule-based structure score
outcome: Best overall 37.9/100 (o3-deep-research); level peaks Recognition 59.5, Calculation 44.6, Abstraction 44.8, Interpretation 20.3; market-performance section max 17.0

informs_decision: Analyst work grades best where it decomposes into recognition and calculation items; interpretation stays near 20/100 for frontier agents and its grading is LLM-made criteria with no human-agreement figure. Supports grading S1's framework through checkable sub-claims

citation: Hu, Jiao, Liu, Ren, Wen and 18 others (2025), ICLR 2026; arXiv 2509.13160v1 (FinSearchComp). Read: abstract page

citation: Goldsack, Wang, Lin & Chen (2024), arXiv 2410.01039v1 (From Facts to Insights). Read: abstract page and v1 HTML
text_source: 60 earnings-call transcripts (ECTSum); 26 J.P. Morgan analyst reports (2012-2016) as references
feature: Multi-agent analytical reports from earnings calls; graded on 5 dimensions (takeaways, context, management attitude, expectations, future events)
method: GPT-4 (AutoGen) agents; 3 finance postgraduate raters; GPT-4, Gemini-pro, Mistral-medium as judges
outcome: Rater agreement kappa 0.171 (0.476 merging top labels); experts preferred analyst reports 83.3%; judge-human correlation avg Pearson 0.31-0.51; GPT-4 and Gemini preferred generated reports 70.8-100% of the time in both orders
informs_decision: Holistic grading of analyst write-ups is unreliable even between human raters, and LLM judges favour model-written reports. Do not grade S1's framework holistically

citation: Liu, He, Ou, Zhu, Guo, Peng & Ananiadou (2026), arXiv 2606.08345v1 (AuditFraudBench; work in progress). Read: abstract page and v1 HTML
text_source: 84 AAER cases matched to 295 original and restated 10-K/10-Q/20-F filings
feature: Profit-source attribution (34), misleading-narrative detection (294), fraud-pattern class (295; 5 classes)
method: GPT-5.5, GPT-4.1, DeepSeek-V4, Qwen3-8B/32B with and without reasoning; accuracy, F1, ROUGE on explanations
outcome: Task 1 accuracy 0.97-1.00 for all and task 2 0.04-0.25 (each task has a single gold class); task 3 accuracy 0.43-0.52, Qwen3-8B 0.505 vs GPT-5.5 0.522

citation: Wang, Ji, Wang, Mansi, Lu & Chen (2026), arXiv 2610.24268v1 (From SEC Filings to Financial Signals). Read: abstract page and v1 HTML
text_source: 45,964 10-Q filing events 2001-2024: MD&A text, fundamental ranks, pre-filing analyst forecasts, abnormal returns
feature: Return ranking from disclosure under five information views; next-quarter EPS forecasts, direct and consensus-anchored
method: 13 open models 7B-32B zero-shot, incl. finance-tuned Fino1-14B, Fin-o1-8B, Fin-R1-7B, Llama-Fin-8B, ODA-Fin-RL-8B
outcome: Event-date RankIC 0.025-0.075 (Qwen3-32B 0.074, ODA-Fin-RL-8B 0.072, Qwen2.5-7B 0.052); next-day 0.02-0.05; finance models no reliable next-day advantage; scale mixed; direct EPS forecasts at the 43.4th percentile of analysts (36.6-49.3)
